Missing or malformed argument gives null; empty text gives 0.

features.name: precedent_comment_share
features.definition: What proportion of counter-argument comments cite a specific, functioning institutional precedent (a real existing law, policy, court, organization or system that operates or has operated in practice) in support of their point?
features.spec: Parse OC_comments (JSON list of comments by other users). For each comment decide if the commenter themselves cites at least one specific, concrete institutional precedent as support: a named or clearly identifiable real law, policy, institution, country/state/city program or system that actually functions/functioned in practice (e.g. 'Portugal's decriminalization has reduced overdoses'). Hypothetical institutions, vague appeals ('some countries'), purely abstract principles, and anecdotes with no institution do not count. Quotations of others count only if the commenter adopts them as support. Use title/argument only to interpret the comment's target. Ignore any text announcing OP view change, delta awards, or outcome reports; these are not evidence. Output = number of qualifying comments / total comments, in [0,1]. Empty list -> null; malformed/missing -> null.

features.name: op_argument_has_first_person_singular
features.definition: Does the original argument text contain at least one explicit first-person singular pronoun (I, me, my, mine, myself)?
features.spec: Python: import re; df['op_argument_has_first_person_singular'] = df['argument'].apply(lambda s: None if not isinstance(s,str) else int(bool(re.search(r"\b(?:I|me|my|mine|myself|I'm|I've|I'd|I'll)\b", s)))). Case-sensitive 'I' (so the word 'i' lowercase is ignored); me/my/mine/myself matched case-insensitively is acceptable via (?i:me|my|mine|myself). Contractions I'm/I've/I'd/I'll count (the apostrophe splits tokens so \bI\b matches them). Missing/non-string argument -> null; empty string -> 0. Counts pronouns anywhere in the argument, including inside quotations or edits (mechanical match, not semantically filtered).

features.name: counterarg_cognitive_complexity
features.definition: Across the counter-argument comments, how cognitively complex is the reasoning on average (differentiating multiple perspectives or considerations and integrating them), rated 1-5?
features.spec: Parse OC_comments (JSON list of comments by users other than OP). Use title/argument only to interpret the target. For each comment, rate cognitive complexity of the commenter's own reasoning on 1-5: 1=single undifferentiated assertion, no nuance; 2=simple reasoning with one consideration; 3=acknowledges more than one consideration or perspective or a qualification; 4=differentiates several perspectives/conditions and weighs them; 5=differentiates and integrates multiple perspectives into a coherent higher-level synthesis. Return the mean rating across comments as a single number. Ignore quoted text from others unless the commenter adopts it. Ignore any OP view-change/delta-award announcements, post-outcome updates and reports of the outcome as evidence. Empty list gives null; malformed or missing input gives null.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Discussions where the original argument includes explicit comparisons to established scientific or historical norms are associated with lower view change than those without such comparisons.
hypotheses.h0: Discussions whose argument has explicit comparisons to established scientific or historical norms (argument_compares_to_science_history_norms=1) have the same view-change (delta) rate as those without.
hypotheses.h1: Discussions with argument_compares_to_science_history_norms=1 have lower view-change (delta) rate than those with 0.
hypotheses.note: Association only. Operational assumption: 'established scientific or historical norms' is judged by the LLM from the OP's argument text alone; title excluded. Current argument text may contain edits or outcome announcements (contamination/timing risk); the prompt ignores them, but deleting edits cannot recover original text. Linear probability model on binary delta.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Arguments expressing explicit fear of social rejection or isolation are associated with lower view-change rates than arguments stating beliefs without emotional self-defense.
hypotheses.h0: Rows with explicit_fear_social_rejection have the same or higher delta rate than rows with belief_without_emotional_self_defense.
hypotheses.h1: Rows with explicit_fear_social_rejection have a lower delta rate than rows with belief_without_emotional_self_defense.
hypotheses.note: Both comparison groups are measured. With both included, the fear coefficient is relative to the omitted group (other emotional self-defense without social-rejection fear), not directly versus plain belief statements; the contrast beta_fear - beta_plain is not a single design-matrix term, so the test is only approximate. hypotheses.hypothesis: Discussions containing multi-turn reply interactions in the conversation text are associated with a higher likelihood of the original poster changing their view.

hypotheses.h1: Rows with has_multi_turn_exchange = 1 have a higher likelihood of OP view change than rows with has_multi_turn_exchange = 0.
hypotheses.note: Operational assumption: "multi-turn reply interaction" is measured as at least two distinct speakers in the conversation text with some speaker taking 2+ turns. Reply timing and reply links are unknown and not inferred from speaker order; repeated turns may include non-OP speakers only and may not be direct replies. Conversation text can include later replies and explicit view-change/delta announcements (outcome contamination risk): turn structure may itself reflect the outcome (e.g., OP thanks/delta turns), and the raw-text code does not filter this. Header regex could misparse bracketed text. Association only, not causal.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Posts containing a single, highly-rated counterargument are associated with an increased frequency of attribution replies from the original poster.
hypotheses.h0: Posts with a single highly-rated counterargument show no difference in the frequency of OP attribution replies compared with other posts.
hypotheses.h1: Posts with a single highly-rated counterargument show a higher frequency of OP attribution replies.
hypotheses.note: Unsupported, so term=null. (1) The claim needs per-comment ratings to identify a single highly-rated counterargument. OC_comments has no comment scores, and post_score is the score of the original post, not of a comment. (2) The claim's outcome is the frequency of OP attribution replies, which is not the dataset target delta. Attribution replies are also probably tied to delta-award or view-change announcements, so a predictor built from them would reveal the outcome. (3) conversation has no reliable reply timing or reply links. I used no substitute proxies, such as comment count or post_score.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Discussions where the original argument contains explicit self-referential meta-commentary regarding platform mechanics or author status are associated with a lower probability of view change.
hypotheses.h0: op_meta_commentary_platform_or_status has no association with the probability of view change (delta).
hypotheses.h1: op_meta_commentary_platform_or_status is associated with a lower probability of view change (delta).
hypotheses.note: Associational test via OLS (linear probability). Argument text is current text and may include edits/outcome announcements; these are excluded from the semantic judgment but timing cannot be established. 'Author status' operationalized as the OP referring to themselves as poster/newcomer/OP; this interpretation is an assumption.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Discussions where counter-argument comments include direct quotes from the original argument are more frequently associated with a changed view than those without such quotations.
hypotheses.h0: Changed-view rate does not differ by any_comment_quotes_op_argument.
hypotheses.h1: Discussions with any_comment_quotes_op_argument=1 have a higher rate of changed view than those with 0.
hypotheses.note: Association only. OLS on binary delta is a linear probability model. Comments are unordered with no timestamps; the OP's argument is current text and may include edits, so quotes may match later-edited text. Quotation marks alone don't establish a quote from the OP; the model checks against argument.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Posts with observed scores below the median are associated with a lower probability of the original poster changing their view compared to higher-scored posts.
hypotheses.h0: post_score_below_median has no association with the probability that the OP changed their view (delta).
hypotheses.h1: Posts with post_score_below_median = 1 have a lower probability of OP view change than posts with post_score_below_median = 0.
hypotheses.note: Median is computed over the supplied 2,000-row corpus (not an external population). Posts exactly at the median fall in the comparison (higher/equal) group; if many ties exist, this group is not strictly 'higher-scored'. post_score measurement time relative to the outcome is unknown, and the score may reflect or follow the view change/discussion, so this is an association only, not causal or prospective. Linear probability model via OLS. post_created_utc does not establish score timing.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Discussions where counter-arguments use second-person direct address to the original poster are associated with a higher likelihood of view change.
hypotheses.h0: share_comments_direct_address_op has no association with the likelihood of OP view change.
hypotheses.h1: Higher share_comments_direct_address_op is associated with a higher likelihood of OP view change.
hypotheses.note: Operationalized as the share of counter-argument comments with direct second-person address to OP (the hypothesis does not specify any/share; share chosen). Distinguishing OP-directed from generic 'you' requires interpretation. Comments may include later replies or outcome text (comment timing unknown); semantic exclusions are applied. Association only, not causal. OLS on binary outcome is a linear probability model.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Discussions where the original poster's argument contains a direct plea for non-violация are associated with a lower likelihood of view change.

hypotheses.note: The hypothesis text contains a garbled token ('non-violация'); it is interpreted as 'non-violence'. The current argument text may include edits or outcome announcements; the prompt excludes them, but timing is not verifiable and no edit timestamps exist. Association only, not causal. hypotheses.hypothesis: Higher cognitive complexity in counterarguments is associated with a higher likelihood of the original poster changing their stated view in ChangeMyView discussions.

hypotheses.note: Cognitive complexity is not defined in the hypothesis; the 1-5 rubric (differentiation and integration) and mean aggregation across comments are operational assumptions. Outcome is binary delta, fitted with OLS (linear probability). Association only, not causal. hypotheses.hypothesis: Discussions where counter-arguments explicitly acknowledge the original poster's underlying valid point before introducing the discrepancy are associated with higher view-change rates than pure refutations.

Association only, not causal.

Operational assumption: OP examples/anecdotes are identified from current title/argument text, which may include edits or outcome announcements (excluded from semantic judgments, but timing is unknown). Comparison requires both named groups, so rows with neither or both term types are dropped (missing values removed by OLS), leaving a reduced sample. Title is current supplied text; possible outcome contamination is not filtered. Association only, not causal.

right_feature.spec: Parse OC_comments (JSON list of comments by users other than the OP). Use title and argument only to interpret what the OP's claim is. For each comment decide whether the commenter's OWN asserted first-person experience or concrete personal story (specific event/situation they or people close to them lived through) is used to illustrate real-world consequences relevant to the OP's claim. Quoted or cited others' experiences, hypotheticals, generic examples and abstract/theoretical arguments do not count unless the commenter adopts them as their own account. Ignore any text announcing that the OP changed their view, delta awards, or post-outcome updates; these are not evidence. Output = (number of qualifying comments)/(total comments), between 0 and 1. Null if the list is missing or malformed or empty.

left_feature.name: abstract_principle_comment_share
left_feature.definition: What proportion of counter-argument comments rely on abstract normative principles (e.g. rights, fairness, morality, what ought to be) rather than specific institutional precedents?
left_feature.spec: Parse OC_comments. For each comment decide if its main support is an abstract normative principle or value argument (e.g. fairness, liberty, justice, moral duty, 'people should') without citing a specific, functioning institutional precedent as its support. A comment that cites a specific functioning institutional precedent as its main support does not count; comments with neither (e.g. purely factual/personal/logical) do not count. Commenter's own assertions only; quotations count only if adopted. Use title/argument only to interpret the target. Ignore any OP view-change/delta announcements or outcome reports. Output = qualifying comments / total comments, in [0,1]. Empty list -> null; malformed/missing -> null.

right_feature.spec: Parse OC_comments (JSON list of other users' comments); use title and argument only to interpret the OP's view. Return 1 if at least one comment, in its own assertions, offers substantive opposition to the OP's view: gives reasons, evidence, examples or logic against it. Bare disagreement, insults, jokes, questions only, or supportive comments do not count. Quoted text counts only if the commenter adopts it. Ignore any OP view-change/delta-award announcements, post-outcome updates, or reports of the outcome as evidence. Return 0 if comments exist but none qualify; 0 for an empty list; null if OC_comments is missing or malformed.

left_feature.name: abstract_principle_comment_share
left_feature.definition: What proportion of counter-argument comments rely on abstract normative principles (e.g. rights, fairness, morality, what ought to be) rather than specific institutional precedents?
left_feature.spec: Parse OC_comments. For each comment decide if its main support is an abstract normative principle or value argument (e.g. fairness, liberty, justice, moral duty, 'people should') without citing a specific, functioning institutional precedent as its support. A comment that cites a specific functioning institutional precedent as its main support does not count; comments with neither (e.g. purely factual/personal/logical) do not count. Commenter's own assertions only; quotations count only if adopted. Use title/argument only to interpret the target. Ignore any OP view-change/delta announcements or outcome reports. Output = qualifying comments / total comments, in [0,1]. Empty list -> null; malformed/missing -> null.

right_feature.spec: Read only the `argument` text (OP's own explanation). Return 1 if the OP's own assertions include at least one personal anecdote or first-person experiential narrative (e.g., describing something that happened to them or that they personally did/experienced/witnessed). Return 0 if none. Do not count quotations or stories attributed to other people/sources unless the OP adopts them as their own experience; quotation marks alone do not establish another speaker. Do not count purely abstract opinions, hypotheticals, or general claims. Ignore and do not count OP view-change/delta-award announcements, post-outcome edits/resolution updates, or reports of the outcome as anecdotes. Return null if argument is missing or malformed; empty text gives 0.

left_feature.definition: Does the original post explicitly invite critique or counterarguments, or frame its own claims with tentative/hedged language?
left_feature.spec: Read title and argument (OP's own text). Return 1 if the OP's own assertions explicitly invite critique/counterarguments/being challenged (e.g., 'point out where I'm wrong', 'convince me') or frame the main view with tentative language (e.g., 'I think', 'maybe', 'seems', 'to my knowledge', 'I'm not sure'). Return 0 if neither appears. Generic CMV boilerplate in the title prefix 'CMV:' alone does not count. Ignore quoted text from others unless OP adopts it. Ignore any OP view-change/delta-award announcements, post-outcome edits or reports of the outcome. Return null if both fields are missing/empty.

right_feature.name: comment_acknowledges_premise_then_diverges
right_feature.definition: Does at least one counter-argument comment explicitly acknowledge the validity of the original post's initial premise before introducing divergence from it?
right_feature.spec: Parse OC_comments (JSON list of comments by users other than the OP). Use title and argument only to identify the OP's initial premise/claim. Return 1 if at least one single comment both (a) explicitly acknowledges that the OP's initial premise (or its starting premise/basic point) is valid, correct, reasonable or true, in the commenter's own voice (not merely quoting the OP or a third party without adopting it), and (b) afterwards within that same comment introduces a point of disagreement or divergence (e.g. 'but', 'however', a different consideration). Acknowledgment must come before the divergence in the comment text. Both conditions must co-occur in the same comment; separate comments cannot jointly satisfy it. Return 0 if no comment qualifies, including generic politeness without validating the premise, or agreement with no divergence. Empty comment list gives 0; missing/malformed OC_comments gives null. Ignore any text announcing that the OP changed their view, delta awards, or post-outcome resolution updates; do not treat them as evidence. Generic discussion of delta/platform rules is eligible but is not itself acknowledgment of the premise.

left_feature.spec: Parse OC_comments (JSON list of comments by users other than the OP). Use title and argument only to interpret each comment's target. For each comment, decide whether its main support is abstract reasoning (general principles, logical argument, definitions, conceptual distinctions, hypotheticals) with no concrete real-world example carrying the argument. Comments that primarily rest on a concrete real-world example do not count. Quoted text from others counts as the commenter's reasoning only if adopted. Ignore any OP view-change/delta-award announcements, post-outcome updates or reports of the outcome as evidence. Output = number of such comments / total comments, in [0,1]. Empty list -> null; missing or malformed -> null.

right_feature.name: any_direct_counterargument
right_feature.definition: Does at least one comment by another user directly argue against the OP's stated view or its reasoning?
right_feature.spec: Parse OC_comments (JSON list of other users' comments). Use title and argument only to identify the OP's view and each comment's target. Return 1 if at least one comment, in its own assertions, directly challenges the OP's central claim or a specific premise/reasoning step (e.g., gives a counterexample, contrary evidence, or a reasoned objection). Return 0 if comments exist but none does (e.g., only agreement, clarifying questions, jokes, off-topic or meta remarks). Quoted text counts only if the commenter adopts it as their own objection. Ignore any OP view-change or delta-award announcements, post-outcome resolution updates and reports of the outcome as evidence; do not treat them or thanks for changing a view as counterarguments. Empty list gives 0; missing or malformed OC_comments gives null.

right_feature.spec: Parse OC_comments (JSON list of comments by users other than the OP). Use title and argument only to interpret what the OP's claim is. For each comment decide whether the commenter's OWN asserted first-person experience or concrete personal story (specific event/situation they or people close to them lived through) is used to illustrate real-world consequences relevant to the OP's claim. Quoted or cited others' experiences, hypotheticals, generic examples and abstract/theoretical arguments do not count unless the commenter adopts them as their own account. Ignore any text announcing that the OP changed their view, delta awards, or post-outcome updates; these are not evidence. Output = (number of qualifying comments)/(total comments), between 0 and 1. Null if the list is missing or malformed or empty.

right_feature.spec: Parse OC_comments (JSON list of comments by users other than OP). Use title and argument only to interpret what the OP's components are. Return 1 if at least one single comment, in its own assertions (not merely quoted text from others), both (a) explicitly acknowledges that a specific identifiable component (a claim, premise or point) of the OP's argument is valid/correct/fair, and (b) AFTER that acknowledgment in the same comment presents a counter-example (a concrete case or instance that challenges the OP's view). Return 0 if the list is valid and no comment qualifies, including an empty list. Return null if OC_comments is missing or malformed. right_feature.spec: Read only the `argument` text (OP's own words). Return 1 if the OP, in their own assertions (not quoted text attributed to others unless the OP adopts it), explicitly comments on the discussion platform's mechanics (e.g., subreddit rules, how deltas/points work, moderation, posting format, downvotes/karma, being new or a throwaway account) or on their own status as author/poster (e.g., 'I'm new here', 'first time posting', 'as OP'). Return 0 otherwise. Generic platform-rule discussion counts. EXCLUDE as evidence: OP announcements of view change, delta awards, edits reporting outcome or post-outcome resolution updates (e.g., 'EDIT: view changed, delta given'). Do not count ordinary topical argument content. Empty or missing argument gives null. Current text only; edits cannot be separated by time.

left_feature.name: anecdote_comment_share
left_feature.definition: What proportion of the counter-argument comments employ a concrete personal anecdote (the commenter's own specific experience) to argue against the OP?
left_feature.spec: Parse OC_comments (JSON list of comments by users other than the OP). For each comment decide whether the commenter themself relates a concrete, specific personal anecdote/experience (particular events, people or situations they lived through) as part of their counter-argument. Use title/argument only to interpret what the comment is responding to. Do not count hypotheticals, generic examples, or others' stories/quotations unless the commenter adopts them as their own experience. Ignore any text announcing that the OP changed their view, delta awards, or post-outcome resolution updates; these are not evidence. Output = (number of comments meeting the criterion)/(total comments), a float in [0,1]. Empty list -> null; missing/malformed -> null.

right_feature.spec: Parse OC_comments (JSON list of other users' comments). Quotes of other sources or of other commenters do not count. Return 0 if no comment does. Empty list gives 0; missing or malformed OC_comments or argument gives null. Do not count OP view-change/delta-award announcements or outcome reports as evidence; ignore such text when judging quotes.

right_feature.spec: Parse OC_comments (JSON list of comments by users other than OP). left_feature.spec: Parse OC_comments (JSON list of comments by users other than OP). right_feature.spec: Parse OC_comments; use title and argument to interpret the OP's view. Return 1 if the list is nonempty and every comment's own assertions support or agree with the OP's view, with no comment offering counterargument or opposition. Return 0 if at least one comment is opposing, neutral/off-topic-only mixes that include any opposing comment, or if comments are not all supportive. Comments that are neutral and not opposing count as not supportive (return 0 unless all are supportive). Ignore OP view-change/delta-award announcements, post-outcome updates and outcome reports as evidence. Empty list or missing/malformed input: null.

left_feature.name: counterarg_cognitive_complexity
left_feature.definition: Across the counter-argument comments, how cognitively complex is the reasoning on average (differentiating multiple perspectives or considerations and integrating them), rated 1-5?
left_feature.spec: Parse OC_comments (JSON list of comments by users other than OP). Use title/argument only to interpret the target. For each comment, rate cognitive complexity of the commenter's own reasoning on 1-5: 1=single undifferentiated assertion, no nuance; 2=simple reasoning with one consideration; 3=acknowledges more than one consideration or perspective or a qualification; 4=differentiates several perspectives/conditions and weighs them; 5=differentiates and integrates multiple perspectives into a coherent higher-level synthesis. Return the mean rating across comments as a single number. Ignore quoted text from others unless the commenter adopts it. Ignore any OP view-change/delta-award announcements, post-outcome updates and reports of the outcome as evidence. Empty list gives null; malformed or missing input gives null.

right_feature.name: any_specific_empirical_counterargument

right_feature.spec: Parse OC_comments (JSON list of other users' comments). Use title and argument only to understand what the OP's view is. Return 1 if at least one comment, in its own assertion, argues against the OP's view and cites a specific empirical example as support (a named or concretely described real-world case, event, study, statistic or data point; an external source cited as support counts). Return 0 if no comment does (only abstract reasoning, hypotheticals, generic claims, or opinion). Ignore quoted OP text and quotations of others unless the commenter adopts them as support. Exclude OP view-change or delta-award announcements, post-outcome resolution updates and reports of the outcome; these are not evidence. Empty list gives 0; missing or malformed OC_comments gives null.

right_feature.spec: Parse OC_comments (JSON list of comments by other users). Use title/argument only to interpret what a comment targets. For each comment decide whether the commenter's own argument includes at least one concrete, specific, checkable example (named or specific case, event, instance, figure, or described particular situation that can be verified locally within the comment/context), not merely a general principle or hypothetical. An external source or case cited as support counts; quoted OP text or quoted background that the commenter does not adopt does not. Ignore any statements that the OP changed their view, delta awards, or post-outcome resolution updates; they are not evidence. Output = (comments meeting the criterion)/(total comments), range 0-1. Empty list -> null; malformed/missing -> null.

left_feature.name: any_validates_emotion_before_rebuttal
left_feature.definition: Does at least one counter-argument comment explicitly validate the OP's emotional experience before giving a logical rebuttal in that same comment?
left_feature.spec: Parse OC_comments (JSON list of other users' comments). Use title and argument only to interpret what the OP's emotional experience is. Return 1 if at least one single comment explicitly acknowledges or validates the OP's feelings/emotional experience (e.g., 'I understand why you feel frustrated', 'that sounds painful') in its own words, and this validation appears earlier in the comment than that comment's logical rebuttal/counter-argument to the OP's view. Both elements must occur in the same comment; separate comments cannot combine. Validation of only the argument's logic, generic politeness, or quoted text not adopted by the commenter does not count. Ignore any OP view-change/delta announcements, post-outcome updates, or reports of the outcome as evidence. Return 0 if no comment qualifies, including when the list is valid but empty; null if OC_comments is missing or malformed.

For each comment decide whether, within that same comment, the commenter first explicitly acknowledges that the OP's position/reasoning has validity (e.g. 'you're right that...', 'this is a fair point') AND THEN introduces a narrower, specific caveat, exception or qualification (not a blanket rejection). Use title and argument only to interpret the comment's target. Acknowledgement of something other than the OP's view, or acknowledgement without a following specific caveat, does not count. Ignore quoted text unless the commenter adopts it. Exclude any OP view-change/delta-award announcements, post-outcome updates and reports of the outcome as evidence. Output = (number of qualifying comments)/(total comments), a number in [0,1]. Empty list -> null; malformed/missing -> null.

right_feature.name: share_comments_with_numerical_data
right_feature.definition: What proportion of the counter-argument comments contain specific numerical data or statistics (as opposed to only general assertions)?
right_feature.spec: Parse OC_comments (JSON list of comments by users other than the OP). For each comment decide whether the commenter's own text presents specific numerical data or statistics as support (e.g., concrete figures, percentages, rates, counts, study results with numbers, dated quantitative facts), including numbers attributed to a cited external source. Do not count vague quantifiers ('many', 'most'), numbers that are not evidential data (list numbering, 'two reasons', times/dates used only as labels, usernames), or purely hypothetical made-up numbers. Exclude any text that announces an OP view change/delta award or reports the discussion outcome; delta-rule discussion is eligible but is not itself numerical evidence. Return number of comments meeting this divided by total number of comments, a value in [0,1]. Empty list gives null; malformed input gives null.
